vegetable nitrate intake is inversely associated with cardiovascular mortality in older men and women, independent of lifestyle, dietary and cardiovascular risk factors.

in a large cohort of older Australian men and older women we found that higher vegetable nitrate intake (from vegetables, not dietary supplements) was associated with a reduced hazard of cardiovascular disease mortality, after adjustment for age, sex, smoking status, alcohol intake, physical activity, body mass index and other lifestyle factors, as well as for cardiovascular risk factors such as hypertension, hyperlipidemia, diabetes and prior history of cardiovascular disease.
